mainTopic: Which men's relations disqualify a woman from כהונה and תרומה, how we learn it, and the start of a new משנה
overview: The גמרא reads the פסוק about a כהן's daughter who is widowed or divorced (ויקרא 22:13). Widowhood and divorce only exist with a man she can marry, so a גוי or an עבד disqualifies her even without a child. The extra word 'ובת' shows the same is true for a לויה and a ישראלית, and even the רבנן agree. According to רבי עקיבא, the words אלמנה and גרושה teach two other laws: a widow with a child may not return to eat תרומה, and a divorcée without a child may. The words 'איש זר' show that a man who remarries his divorcée does not disqualify her. A חלל does disqualify her, because the פסוק compares him to his father. The case of a כהן גדול with an אלמנה shows that relations alone disqualify her, without קידושין. The גמרא then explains how the תנא קמא, רבי יוסי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל differ: over a second-generation מצרי, and over a גר עמוני or מואבי. A new משנה begins: a rapist, a seducer and a שוטה do not affect a woman's right to eat תרומה, unless the man may not marry into ישראל.

steps.title: Only a man who can marry her has widowhood and divorce
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק talks about a man with whom widowhood and divorce are possible. That leaves out a גוי and an עבד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק means a man who can have widowhood and divorce with her. This excludes a גוי and an עבד, who cannot have widowhood and divorce with her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a reading of the פסוק. Since the פסוק says 'widow or divorced', it must be talking about a man who can legally marry her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גוי or עבד cannot marry a Jewish woman, so she can never be his widow or his divorcee. The פסוק's rule that she goes back to her father's house when there is no child applies only to a real husband. So a גוי or עבד disqualifies her even without a child.

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ אַלְמְנוּת וְגֵירוּשִׁין בָּהּ,
phrases.english: One who can have widowhood and divorce with her,
phrases.notes: This is explaining the words 'widow or divorced' in ויקרא 22:13.

phrases.english: excluding a gentile and a slave
who cannot have widowhood and divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ אַלְמְנוּת וְגֵירוּשִׁין בָּהּ, יָצְאוּ גּוֹי וְעֶבֶד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a derivation that began before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'widow or divorced' clause refers only to a man who can marry her. A גוי and an עבד are excluded, so they disqualify her even without a child.

steps.title: What about a Levite or Israelite woman?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק talks about a כהנת. Where do we learn the same rule for a לויה or ישראלית?
steps.simpleTranslation: We have found the source for a כהנת. For a לויה and a ישראלית, where do we learn it from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the פסוק only mentions a כהן's daughter. It asks for a source that the rule also covers other Jewish women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The derivation in step 1 was built on 'בת כהן', a כהן's daughter. The question is whether a לויה or ישראלית is disqualified the same way by a גוי or עבד.

phrases.english: We have found it for a priest's daughter;
a Levite and an Israelite woman, from where do we know?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחַן כֹּהֶנֶת — לְוִיָּה וְיִשְׂרְאֵלִית מְנָא לַן?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to extend the rule from step 1 to other women
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that a לויה and a ישראלית are also disqualified by a גוי or עבד

steps.title: The extra 'and' in 'and a daughter' adds other women
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא quotes רב: the פסוק could have said 'בת' but says 'ובת'. The extra word adds a לויה and a ישראלית.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי אבא said in the name of רב: the פסוק could have said 'a daughter' but says 'and a daughter'. Here too, 'a daughter' versus 'and a daughter' teaches us to add more women.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a teaching of רב. The extra letter ו at the start of 'ובת' brings in women who are not a כהן's daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב uses the same kind of learning elsewhere, and the גמרא says to apply it here too. The ו, meaning 'and', adds to the case the פסוק names. So the rule for a כהנת also covers a לויה and a ישראלית.

keyTerms.meaning: and a daughter (with the extra ו)

phrases.english: As Rabbi Abba said that Rav said:
'a daughter', 'and a daughter',
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:13 starts with 'ובת', 'and a daughter'. That 'and' looks extra, so it comes to add another case.

phrases.english: here too: 'a daughter', 'and a daughter'.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב: ״בַּת״ ״וּבַת״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra ו in 'ובת' adds a לויה and a ישראלית

steps.title: Does this only work for רבי עקיבא?
steps.stepSummary: Learning from a single letter ו is the method of רבי עקיבא. Does the answer only work according to him?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom is this? Only according to רבי עקיבא, who learns laws from the letter ו?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 3. Not everyone learns laws from a single extra ו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא learns from every extra ו, but the רבנן do not. If the source rests only on the ו, then the רבנן would have no source for a לויה and a ישראלית.

keyTerms.meaning: the תנא who learns even from small extra letters
learns laws from the letter ו

phrases.english: According to whom? According to Rabbi Akiva
who learns from the letter vav?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן — כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא דְּדָרֵישׁ וָוֵי?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the method used in step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation from the extra ו in 'ובת'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only רבי עקיבא learns from a single ו, so the רבנן would be left with no source

steps.title: Even the Rabbis agree, because the whole word is extra
steps.stepSummary: Even the רבנן can learn it, since the entire word 'ובת' is extra in the פסוק, not just the ו.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say this follows the רבנן: the whole phrase 'ובת' is an extra word in the פסוק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the source. It is not built on one letter but on a whole extra word, and everyone learns from that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier פסוקים already spoke about a כהן's daughter, so writing 'ובת' again is completely extra. Even the רבנן, who do not learn from a lone ו, learn from a whole extra word.

keyTerms.meaning: the Sages who disagree with רבי עקיבא
an extra, unneeded word in the פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: A גוי or עבד disqualifies a לויה and a ישראלית too. Even the רבנן agree, because the whole word 'ובת' is extra.

phrases.english: You can even say it follows the Rabbis:
the whole 'and a daughter' is an extra word in the verse.
phrases.notes: Earlier פסוקים already spoke about a כהן's daughter, so the whole word is extra here.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּנַן — כּוּלֵּהּ ״וּבַת״ קְרָא יַתִּירָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Widens the base of the derivation from one letter to a whole extra word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The source depends only on the ו, so it works only for רבי עקיבא
steps.terutzMaskana: The whole word 'ובת' is extra, so the רבנן agree too

steps.title: Maybe the verse means the opposite: with a non-husband she may eat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests another reading. Perhaps a child disqualifies her only from a real husband, and with a גוי or עבד she may eat even if there is a child.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say instead: with one who can have widowhood and divorce with her, if he has no child from her she eats, and if he has a child she does not eat. With one who cannot have widowhood and divorce with her, she should eat even if he has a child!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different reading of 'widow or divorced'. That reading would make a גוי or עבד less harmful, not more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 read the פסוק as saying that a גוי or עבד disqualifies her even without a child. The new suggestion flips it: the פסוק's rules about a child apply only to a real husband. A child from a גוי or עבד, who is not counted as his, would not stop her from eating תרומה.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not the conclusion. It is a suggestion that challenges the reading in step 1, and the גמרא will deal with it next.

phrases.english: But say: one who has
widowhood and divorce with her,
when he has no child, she eats,
phrases.notes: 'Eats' means eating תרומה after she is widowed or divorced.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אִית לֵיהּ זֶרַע — לָא אָכְלָה.
phrases.english: when he has a child, she does not eat.

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אַלְמְנוּת וְגֵירוּשִׁין בָּהּ,
phrases.english: One who does not have widowhood and divorce with her,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִית לֵיהּ זֶרַע
phrases.english: even though he has a child
she should also eat!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ אַלְמְנוּת וְגֵירוּשִׁין בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the reading in step 1 and offers a reversed one
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation in step 1 that a גוי or עבד disqualifies her
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same words could mean that the child rule applies only to a real husband, so with a גוי or עבד she may eat even with a child

steps.title: The inclusion of a לויה and ישראלית proves the rule is a stringency
steps.stepSummary: The lenient reading cannot be right, because then there would be no reason to include a לויה and a ישראלית.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why do I need to include a Levite and an Israelite woman?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from step 6 with a short question: if the rule were a leniency, why would the Torah need the extra word to include a לויה and a ישראלית?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a כהנת who was with a גוי or עבד still eats תרומה even with a child, then a לויה or ישראלית obviously would too, and no special word would be needed for them. The Torah did add a word (ובת) to include them. That shows the rule learned here is a new restriction, not a leniency.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if what you suggested were true
To include; to add a case through an extra word in the פסוק
Why do I need it? (Points out that something would be pointless)

phrases.english: If so,
why do I need to include a Levite and an Israelite woman?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, רַבּוֹיֵי לְוִיָּה וְיִשְׂרְאֵלִית לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6 by showing its lenient reading makes the extra word pointless.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the opposing reading would make the extra word ובת unnecessary
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe with a גוי or עבד she may eat תרומה even if she has a child.
steps.terutzMaskana: Including a לויה and a ישראלית only makes sense if the rule is a restriction, so a גוי or עבד does disqualify her.

steps.title: According to רבי עקיבא, why does the פסוק say widow or divorcée?
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא reads 'כי תהיה לאיש זר' as relations, not marriage. Then a גוי and an עבד are already covered, so why does the Torah need the words אלמנה וגרושה?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי עקיבא, who said that betrothal does not take effect with those forbidden by a לאו, and so 'if she be to a common man' means 'if she has relations,' why do I need 'a widow or divorced'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question: according to רבי עקיבא, the words אלמנה וגרושה in the next פסוק seem to have no job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא holds that קידושין do not take effect with someone forbidden by a לאו. So the word 'תהיה' cannot mean marriage, and he reads it as relations. Relations with a גוי or עבד are then already covered by that word, so the words אלמנה וגרושה seem unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: People forbidden to each other by a negative commandment (a לאו)

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Akiva, who said:
betrothal does not take effect
with those forbidden by a negative commandment,
and what does "if she be to a common man" mean?
if she has relations,
why do I need "a widow or divorced"?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:13. These words are from the next פסוק, about when she may return to eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the ובת derivation, the גמרא asks what the words אלמנה וגרושה, used in step 1 to exclude a גוי and an עבד, teach according to רבי עקיבא, who already covers them through 'תהיה'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the words אלמנה וגרושה in the פסוק according to רבי עקיבא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'תהיה' already means relations, then a גוי and an עבד are already covered, so the words אלמנה וגרושה seem to teach nothing.

steps.title: Widow teaches a stringency, divorcée teaches a leniency, and both are needed
steps.stepSummary: אלמנה teaches that a widow with a child may not return to eat, and גרושה teaches that a divorcée without a child may return. Each case could not be learned from the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: A widow is mentioned to be strict with her, and a divorcée to be lenient with her, and both are needed. If the Torah taught only a widow, I would say a widow without a child eats because she may still marry a כהן, but a divorcée, who may not, does not eat even without a child. If it taught only a divorcée, I would say a divorcée with a child does not eat because she may not marry a כהן, but a widow, who may, eats even with a child. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that each word has its own job: אלמנה adds a stringency and גרושה adds a leniency. Then it explains why the Torah had to write both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אלמנה is still allowed to marry a כהן, so I might think she always returns to eat. The word אלמנה teaches that if she has a child, she does not. A גרושה may never marry a כהן, so I might think she never returns. The word גרושה teaches that if she has no child, she does. Each case has its own reason to go the other way, so neither can be learned from the other.

keyTerms.meaning: And both are needed; one cannot be learned from the other
She is fit to marry a כהן

steps.whatToRemember: A widow with a child does not return to eat תרומה, and a divorcée without a child does return. According to רבי עקיבא, this is why the Torah wrote both words: each case has a reason that would have pushed the law the other way.

phrases.english: "A widow" is to be strict with her,
and "divorced" is to be lenient with her.
And both are needed.
For if it had taught us only a widow:

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָנָה הוּא דְּכִי לֵית לַהּ זֶרַע — אָכְלָה,
phrases.english: it is a widow who eats when she has no child,
because she is fit for the כהונה.
But a divorcée, who is not fit for the כהונה,

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֵית לַהּ זֶרַע — לָא אָכְלָה.
phrases.english: I would say: even though she has no child, she does not eat.
And if it had taught us only a divorcée:

phrases.aramaic: גְּרוּשָׁה הוּא דְּכִי אִית לַהּ זֶרַע — לָא אָכְלָה,
phrases.english: it is a divorcée who does not eat when she has a child,
because she is not fit for the כהונה.
But a widow, who is fit for the כהונה,

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִית לַהּ זֶרַע — נָמֵי תֵּיכוֹל,
phrases.english: I would say: even though she has a child, she may also eat.
So both are needed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָנָה לְהַחְמִיר עָלֶיהָ, וּגְרוּשָׁה לְהָקֵל עָלֶיהָ. וּצְרִיכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8 by giving each word its own job.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns each word its own separate teaching, with a צריכא to show both are needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without both words, the widow might always eat or the divorcée might never eat.
steps.terutzMaskana: A widow with a child does not eat, and a divorcée without a child does eat.

steps.title: Does remarrying one's divorcée count as a forbidden partner?
steps.stepSummary: Maybe a man who remarries his גרושה, which is forbidden, also counts as a partner who is forbidden to her and disqualifies her.
steps.simpleTranslation: And say that 'she had relations with a man unfit for her' includes even a man who remarries his divorcée!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about another forbidden partner. A man who takes back his ex-wife after she married someone else is doing something forbidden. Does that also disqualify her?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule so far is that relations with a man forbidden to her disqualify her. A מחזיר גרושתו is forbidden to her too. So the question is whether this rule should cover him as well.

keyTerms.meaning: She had relations with a man who is forbidden to her
A man who remarries his ex-wife after she was married to someone else (forbidden)

phrases.english: And say that "she had relations with a man unfit for her"
includes even one who remarries his divorcée!
phrases.notes: He means a man taking back his ex-wife after she married someone else in between, which the Torah forbids.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא נִבְעֲלָה לְפָסוּל לָהּ אַף מַחְזִיר גְּרוּשָׁתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests how far the category of 'a man forbidden to her' reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: The limits of the category נבעלה לפסול לה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מחזיר גרושתו is also forbidden to her, so he should seem to disqualify her too.

steps.title: Only a man who was a stranger to her from the start disqualifies her
steps.stepSummary: The Torah says 'איש זר', a stranger. This means someone who was forbidden to her from the beginning, not her own ex-husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah says 'to a stranger man': someone who was a stranger to her from the start. This leaves out this man, who was not a stranger to her from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from the word זר in the פסוק: only a man who was always forbidden to her disqualifies her. Her ex-husband was once permitted to her, so he does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word זר means a stranger. Her ex-husband was once her lawful husband, so he was never a stranger to her from the start. That is why the מחזיר גרושתו is left out, even though remarrying her now is forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: 'איש זר' means a man who was forbidden to her from the start, so a man who remarries his divorcée does not disqualify her.

phrases.english: The Torah said "to a stranger man,"
meaning one who was a stranger to her from the start.
This leaves out this one,
for he was not a stranger to her from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״לְאִישׁ זָר״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10 using the word זר in the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reads a precise word in the פסוק to narrow the category
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any forbidden partner, even her own ex-husband, would disqualify her.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a man forbidden to her from the start disqualifies her, so her ex-husband does not.

steps.title: A חלל is not a 'stranger' from the start, so how can he disqualify?
steps.stepSummary: If 'איש זר' means only someone forbidden to her from the beginning, a חלל should not disqualify her.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a חלל, who is not a 'stranger' from the start, should not disqualify her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. If only someone who was forbidden from the start counts as 'איש זר', then a חלל should not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said 'זר' means someone who was forbidden to her from the beginning. A חלל is allowed to marry an ordinary Jewish woman, so he is not forbidden to her from the start. Yet the ברייתא lists him as one who disqualifies her. That is the problem.

keyTerms.meaning: The son of a כֹּהֵן from a marriage forbidden to the כֹּהֵן; he loses כְּהוּנָּה status
If so (introduces a challenge built on what was just said)
From the start, from the beginning

phrases.english: If so, a חלל,
who is not a 'stranger' from the start,
phrases.notes: He means a חלל is not forbidden to an ordinary Jewish woman, so he doesn't fit the definition from the last step.

phrases.english: should not disqualify!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the definition of 'איש זר' given in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'זר' means someone forbidden to her from the start.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A חלל is not forbidden to her from the start, yet he does disqualify her, so the definition seems too narrow.

steps.title: The פסוק compares the son to the father
steps.stepSummary: 'לא יחלל זרעו' compares the כֹּהֵן's son to the כֹּהֵן. Just as the father disqualifies, so does the son.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'He shall not profane his seed among his people.' It compares his seed to him. Just as he disqualifies, so too his seed also disqualifies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a חלל disqualifies because of a separate source. A פסוק compares him to his father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חלל is not included through 'איש זר'. Instead the פסוק links the son ('his seed') to the כֹּהֵן who married wrongly. That כֹּהֵן disqualifies the woman, so his son, the חלל, also disqualifies.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse says (introduces a source from a פָּסוּק)
Compares, links two things through the verse (הֶקֵּשׁ)

phrases.english: The verse says:
"He shall not profane his seed among his people,"
it compares his seed to him.
Just as he disqualifies,
so too his seed also disqualifies.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A חלל should not disqualify, since he is not a 'זר' from the start.
steps.terutzMaskana: A חלל disqualifies because the פסוק compares him to his father, who disqualifies.
steps.whatToRemember: A חלל does not disqualify because he is a 'זר'. He disqualifies because the פסוק links him to his father.

steps.title: Maybe she is disqualified already at the קידושין
steps.stepSummary: Perhaps the woman becomes disqualified as soon as the forbidden man marries her, even before relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say she is disqualified from the time of the betrothal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks a new question: when exactly does the disqualification start? Maybe the קידושין alone is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the topic was relations with a forbidden man. The גמרא suggests that maybe the moment he marries her through קידושין, she is already disqualified, even without ביאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'becoming', meaning becoming his wife through קִידּוּשִׁין

phrases.english: But say from the time of betrothal!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא מִשְּׁעַת הֲוָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from who disqualifies to when the disqualification begins.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that relations are what disqualify her.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'תהיה' could mean marriage, so maybe קידושין alone disqualifies.

steps.title: Like a כהן גדול with a widow, it happens through relations
steps.stepSummary: The case is compared to a כהן גדול with an אלמנה, where the disqualification happens through ביאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like a כהן גדול with an אלמנה. Just as a כהן גדול with an אלמנה disqualifies her through relations, so too this one disqualifies through relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by comparing to a known case, a כהן גדול with a widow, where the woman is disqualified through relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The passage of 'לא יחלל זרעו' (from step 13) is about a כהן גדול and an אלמנה. In that case she is disqualified through ביאה, not through קידושין. The גמרא models every man who disqualifies her on that case, so here too the disqualification comes through ביאה.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow, forbidden to a כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל

phrases.english: It is like a High Priest with a widow:
just as a High Priest with a widow is through relations,
so too this one is also through relations.

steps.triggerLanguage: דּוּמְיָא דְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל בְּאַלְמָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 14.
steps.terutzMaskana: Like the כהן גדול with a widow, the disqualification comes through ביאה.

steps.title: Maybe both קידושין and relations are needed
steps.stepSummary: Perhaps the disqualification requires both marriage and relations together.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say she is not disqualified until there is both betrothal and relations!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one more possibility: maybe she is disqualified only when there is both קידושין and ביאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 showed that ביאה is needed. Now the גמרא asks whether ביאה alone is enough, or whether it must come together with קידושין.

phrases.english: But say: not until there is
betrothal and relations?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: עַד דְּאִיכָּא הֲוָיָה וּבִיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 15 and suggests a stricter requirement.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that ביאה alone disqualifies.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'תהיה' could still matter, so maybe both קידושין and ביאה are needed.

steps.title: Like a כהן גדול with a widow, relations alone are enough
steps.stepSummary: Again the כהן גדול with a widow shows that ביאה alone disqualifies, without קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like a כהן גדול with an אלמנה. Just as a כהן גדול with an אלמנה disqualifies her through relations alone, so too this one disqualifies through relations alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the same comparison again. With a כהן גדול, relations alone disqualify, so here too relations alone are enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same model answers both questions. With a כהן גדול and a widow, she is disqualified even without קידושין, through ביאה only. So קידושין is neither enough by itself nor needed together with ביאה.
steps.whatToRemember: The disqualification comes through ביאה alone. קידושין alone does not disqualify, and קידושין is not needed together with ביאה. This is learned from a כהן גדול with a widow.

phrases.english: It is like a High Priest with a widow:

phrases.aramaic: מָה כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל בְּאַלְמָנָה בְּבִיאָה לְחוּדַּהּ,
phrases.english: just as a High Priest with a widow is through relations alone,
so too this one is also through relations alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: דּוּמְיָא דְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל בְּאַלְמָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 16 with the same comparison.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe both קידושין and ביאה are needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: ביאה alone disqualifies, as with a כהן גדול and a widow.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: whoever's children are unfit disqualifies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי יוסי's opinion from the ברייתא. A man disqualifies her only if his children are unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי says: Anyone whose offspring are unfit disqualifies her. Anyone whose offspring are not unfit does not disqualify her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא and quotes רבי יוסי's opinion. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי gives a general test for which men disqualify a woman. If the children of this man would be unfit, he disqualifies her. If his children would be fit, he does not.

keyTerms.meaning: A תַּנָּא quoted in the בָּרַיְיתָא

phrases.english: And רבי יוסי says:
anyone whose offspring are unfit disqualifies,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל שֶׁאֵין זַרְעוֹ פָּסוּל — אֵינוֹ פּוֹסֵל.
phrases.english: and anyone whose offspring are not unfit does not disqualify.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא to discuss a new opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man disqualifies a woman only if his children would be unfit.

steps.title: How does רבי יוסי differ from the תנא קמא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the first תנא and רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference is there between the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where the two opinions in the ברייתא actually disagree. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's rule sounds like it could match the list of the first תנא. So the גמרא wants to find a real case where the two opinions give different results.

keyTerms.meaning: The first תַּנָּא, the unnamed opinion at the start of the בָּרַיְיתָא

phrases.english: What is there
between the first tanna and רבי יוסי?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין תַּנָּא קַמָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the opinion quoted in step 18 differs from the first תנא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical case where the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי disagree.

steps.title: The difference: a second-generation Egyptian or Edomite
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the first תנא and רבי יוסי disagree about a second-generation מצרי or אדומי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: the difference between them is a מצרי שני and an אדומי שני (a second-generation Egyptian or Edomite).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from the previous step. רבי יוחנן names the exact case where the first תנא and רבי יוסי reach different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A second-generation מצרי or אדומי may not marry into the Jewish people himself, but his children, the third generation, may. So if he has relations with a woman, it is still a forbidden act, yet his children are not unfit. That gap is where the two opinions split.

keyTerms.meaning: A second-generation Egyptian convert: the son of the convert
"There is between them": the practical difference between two opinions

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
A second-generation Egyptian and a second-generation Edomite
phrases.notes: "Second-generation" means the son of the person who converted.

phrases.english: is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מִצְרִי שֵׁנִי וַאֲדוֹמִי שֵׁנִי אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question asked in step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two opinions differ about a second-generation מצרי or אדומי.

steps.title: Both learn from the כהן גדול; the תנא קמא's reasoning
steps.stepSummary: Both opinions come from the case of a כהן גדול with an אלמנה. The first תנא learns that any forbidden act of relations disqualifies her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both of them learned this only from a כהן גדול with an אלמנה. The תנא קמא holds: just as a כהן גדול with an אלמנה, whose relations with her are a sin, disqualifies her, so too this man (the מצרי שני) also disqualifies her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the two opinions differ. It starts with the first תנא's reasoning, and the next step gives רבי יוסי's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions use the same model, the כהן גדול with an אלמנה. The first תנא focuses on the fact that the act was forbidden. Since relations with a second-generation מצרי are also forbidden, he disqualifies her too.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה
Relations that are a sin, meaning a forbidden union
Disqualifies her from marrying a כהן

phrases.english: And both of them learned it only
from a High Priest with a widow.
The first Tanna holds:
Just as a High Priest with a widow,
whose relations are a sin, disqualifies her,
so too this one also disqualifies.
phrases.notes: "This one" is the second-generation Egyptian or Edomite from רבי יוחנן's answer.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁנֵיהֶם לֹא לְמָדוּהָ אֶלָּא מִכֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל בְּאַלְמָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the first side of רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the first תנא, any forbidden act of relations, like that of a כהן גדול with an אלמנה, disqualifies the woman, even with a second-generation מצרי.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's reasoning: only a man whose children are unfit disqualifies
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי learns from the כהן גדול that only a man whose children are unfit disqualifies her. This leaves out the second-generation מצרי, whose children may enter the קהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי holds: it is like a כהן גדול. Just as a כהן גדול, whose children are unfit, disqualifies her, so too anyone whose children are unfit disqualifies her. This excludes a מצרי שני, whose children are not unfit, as it is written: "Children that are born to them, the third generation, may enter into the assembly of ה׳."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יוסי's reasoning from the same model, the כהן גדול. He reaches the opposite result for the second-generation מצרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי focuses on a different feature of the כהן גדול: his children from the אלמנה are unfit. A second-generation מצרי's children are the third generation, and the פסוק says they may join the קהל. So by רבי יוסי's measure, the second-generation מצרי does not disqualify her.

keyTerms.meaning: His children are unfit, with flawed lineage
To exclude: this rule leaves out a certain case
The assembly of ה׳; entering it means being allowed to marry into the Jewish people

steps.whatToRemember: Same source, two different focuses. The first תנא asks whether the act was forbidden. רבי יוסי asks whether his children are unfit. A second-generation מצרי passes the first test but not the second, so he disqualifies only according to the first תנא.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei holds: like a High Priest.

phrases.aramaic: מָה כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל שֶׁזַּרְעוֹ פָּסוּל וּפוֹסֵל,
phrases.english: Just as a High Priest, whose children are unfit, disqualifies,
so too anyone whose children are unfit disqualifies.
This excludes a second-generation Egyptian
whose children are not unfit.
As it is written:
"Children that are born to them,

phrases.aramaic: דּוֹר שְׁלִישִׁי יָבֹא לָהֶם בִּקְהַל ה׳״.
phrases.english: the third generation, may enter into the assembly of ה׳."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי סָבַר: כְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side of the same comparison, completing the explanation of רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, only a man whose children are unfit disqualifies a woman from כהונה, so a second-generation מצרי does not.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's rule: daughter and widow go together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל from the ברייתא: if you may marry a man's daughter, you may marry his widow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: anyone whose daughter you may marry, you may marry his widow, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next opinion in the same ברייתא. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל links the widow's status to the daughter's. If his daughter may marry a כהן, then his relations did not disqualify his widow. If his daughter is unfit, his widow is disqualified too.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא whose opinion appears in the ברייתא

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Anyone whose daughter you may marry,
you may marry his widow, etc.
phrases.notes: The "etc." stands for the rest: if you may not marry his daughter, you may not marry his widow.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: כֹּל שֶׁאַתָּה נוֹשֵׂא בִּתּוֹ אַתָּה נוֹשֵׂא אַלְמְנָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next opinion in the ברייתא, after the first תנא and רבי יוסי have been explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whether his widow may marry a כהן follows whether his daughter may.

steps.title: How does רבי יוסי differ from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between רבי יוסי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference is there between רבי יוסי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how these two opinions differ. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions seem to say the same thing: a man disqualifies a woman only if his children are unfit. So the גמרא wants to know where they would actually rule differently.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between: asks for the practical gap between opinions

steps.confusionAlert: This is a new question. The difference between the first תנא and רבי יוסי was already answered (the second-generation מצרי). Now the גמרא is comparing רבי יוסי with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

phrases.english: What difference is there

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל?
phrases.english: between Rabbi Yosei and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the opinion just quoted differs from רבי יוסי's opinion explained in step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical case where רבי יוסי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל would rule differently, since both seem to tie disqualification to the children's status.

steps.title: עולא: The Difference Is a גר עמוני or מואבי
steps.stepSummary: עולא says the practical difference between רבי יוסי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is a גר עמוני or מואבי. Both of them learn their rule from a כהן גדול with an אלמנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: The difference between them is a גר עמוני or מואבי. Both of them learned their rule only from the case of a כהן גדול with an אלמנה.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the question from Step 24 by naming the case where the two opinions disagree. He also says both opinions come from the same source, which sets up the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions start from the same model case, a כהן גדול with an אלמנה. So the argument must be about which detail of that model counts. The next two steps show how each one reads the model.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the answer here
A convert from the nations of עמון or מואב
There is a difference between them

phrases.english: Ulla said:
An Ammonite or Moabite convert is the difference between them,
and both of them learned it only
from a High Priest with a widow.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: גֵּר עַמּוֹנִי וּמוֹאָבִי אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of Step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two opinions differ over a גר עמוני or מואבי, and both learn from a כהן גדול with an אלמנה.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: Any Man Whose Children Are Unfit Disqualifies
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי learns from a כהן גדול with an אלמנה that any man whose children are unfit disqualifies the woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי holds: A כהן גדול with an אלמנה has unfit children, and he disqualifies her. So too, any man whose children are unfit disqualifies the woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי יוסי reads the model case. All he needs is that the man's children are unfit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, it is enough that the man's children are unfit, even if only some of them. An עמוני's sons are unfit, so under רבי יוסי an עמוני or מואבי does disqualify the woman.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as ... so too (comparing to a model case)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei holds:
Just as a High Priest with a widow,
whose children are unfit, also disqualifies her,
so too, anyone whose children are unfit disqualifies.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי סָבַר: מָה כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל בְּאַלְמָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first half of עולא's answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any man whose children are unfit, even only some of them, disqualifies the woman. This includes an עמוני or מואבי.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: Only If All the Children Are Unfit
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says only a man whose children are ALL unfit disqualifies the woman. This leaves out an עמוני or מואבי, since not all of his children are unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds: All the children of a כהן גדול with an אלמנה are unfit, and he disqualifies her. So too, a man whose children are all unfit disqualifies her. This leaves out an עמוני or מואבי, because not all of his children are unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבן שמעון בן גמליאל reads the same model case. He adds the word 'all', which leaves out the עמוני and מואבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a כהן גדול and an אלמנה, every child is unfit, sons and daughters alike. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל makes that detail the rule. An עמוני's daughters are fit, so he does not disqualify the woman. This is the exact point where he and רבי יוסי part ways.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא whose opinion was quoted in Step 23

steps.confusionAlert: Both rules sound almost the same. The only difference is the word כׇּל, 'all'. רבי יוסי needs only some unfit children. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל needs every child to be unfit.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds:
Just as a High Priest with a widow,
all of whose children are unfit, also disqualifies her,
so too, one all of whose children are unfit disqualifies.
This leaves out an Ammonite or Moabite,
since not all of his children are unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל סָבַר: מָה כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל בְּאַלְמָנָה שֶׁכׇּל זַרְעוֹ פָּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second side of עולא's answer, set against רבי יוסי in Step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a man whose children are all unfit disqualifies the woman. An עמוני or מואבי does not.

steps.title: Source: An עמוני Man Is Unfit, Not an עמונית Woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up the claim that not all of an עמוני's children are unfit. A known teaching says only an עמוני man is forbidden, not an עמונית woman, and the same for מואב.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Master said: 'עמוני' means a man, not an עמונית woman. 'מואבי' means a man, not a מואבית woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source for the fact used in Step 27, that an עמוני's daughters are fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says עמוני and מואבי in the male form. This is read to mean that only the men are forbidden to enter the קהל. So an עמוני's daughters may marry into ישראל, and not all of his children are unfit.

keyTerms.meaning: As the Master said (quoting a known teaching)

steps.whatToRemember: Under רבי יוסי, an עמוני or מואבי disqualifies the woman because his sons are unfit. Under רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, he does not, because his daughters are fit.

phrases.english: As the Master said: 'An Ammonite man,' but not an Ammonite woman,
'A Moabite man,' but not a Moabite woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר מָר: ״עַמּוֹנִי״, וְלֹא עַמּוֹנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the factual claim in Step 27 that not all of an עמוני's children are unfit.
steps.raayaObject: That an עמוני or מואבי does not have all his children unfit.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching עמוני ולא עמונית, מואבי ולא מואבית.

steps.title: New משנה: Rapist, Seducer, and שוטה Do Not Affect תרומה
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. A man who rapes, a man who seduces, and a שוטה neither disqualify a woman from eating תרומה nor give her the right to eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who rapes, one who seduces, and a שוטה do not disqualify a woman from תרומה, and do not enable her to eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a new rule about relations that do not count as a real marriage. These relations do not change a woman's right to eat תרומה in either direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually, marrying a non-כהן stops a בת כהן from eating תרומה, and marrying a כהן lets a woman eat it. Here there is no real marriage, so neither effect happens. A בת כהן keeps eating, and a בת ישראל does not start.

keyTerms.meaning: A person without legal mental capacity

phrases.english: Mishnah:
One who rapes, one who seduces, and an imbecile —
do not disqualify and do not enable to eat.
phrases.notes: He means eating תרומה. A non-כהן doesn't stop her from eating it, and a כהן doesn't give her the right to eat it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאוֹנֵס וְהַמְפַתֶּה וְהַשּׁוֹטֶה לֹא פּוֹסְלִין וְלֹא מַאֲכִילִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Relations with a rapist, a seducer, or a שוטה neither disqualify a woman from תרומה nor let her eat it.

steps.title: Exception: A Man Unfit to Marry Into Israel Does Disqualify
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds an exception. If these men are not allowed to marry into ישראל, their relations do disqualify her.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if they are not fit to enter the assembly of Israel, they do disqualify her.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה limits its first rule. It names a case where even relations without marriage do disqualify the woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Relations without marriage normally have no effect. But a man who is forbidden to marry into ישראל, such as a ממזר, disqualifies the woman through the forbidden act itself. This matches the earlier discussion on the daf about forbidden relations making a woman unfit.

phrases.english: But if they are not fit to enter into Israel —
these do disqualify.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אֵינָן רְאוּיִין לָבֹא בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ פּוֹסְלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to the rule in Step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man who may not marry into ישראל disqualifies the woman, even without marriage.

steps.title: Example: A ישראל With a בת כהן
steps.stepSummary: The משנה begins its examples. If a ישראל has relations with a בת כהן without marriage, she may still eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? If a ישראל had relations with a בת כהן, she may still eat תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה starts showing how its rules work in real cases. This first example is about a regular ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ישראל is allowed to marry into ישראל, and here there was no marriage. So the relations do not disqualify her, and she keeps her right to eat תרומה. This applies the first rule from Step 29.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to כהנים

phrases.english: How so?
An Israelite who had relations with a priest's daughter —
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets (הָיָה, 'there was') and some don't. It doesn't change the meaning.

phrases.english: she may eat teruma.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיצַד? הָיָה יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁבָּא עַל בַּת כֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the examples for the rules in Steps 29–30.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בת כהן who had relations with a ישראל without marriage still eats תרומה.
